= Visual descriptors for building Randland =
== [[Mountains of Mist]] {{ref/book|1|1}}==
The Mountains of Mist rise above the Westwood treetops, distant but in plain sight from Emond's Field. At the foot of the mountains, the Sand Hills flail down into the Westwood. They appear to have heaved out from under a great ocean when the mountains were formed.
* Rose above the Westwood treetops, distant but in plain sight from Emond's Field
== [[Sand Hills]] {{ref/book|1|1}}==
* Once the shore of a great ocean before the mountains heaved out of it during the Breaking of the world
* Flails down into the Two Rivers, into the tangled forest called the Westwood
* At the foot of the Mountains of Mist
== [[Westwood]] {{ref/book|1|1}} {{ref/book|1|5}} ==
A rocky forest with only a handful of farms. The trees become more sparse as they approach the Sand Hills.
==== General ====
* Main character (Rand's) home where he lived with his widowed father
* They made apple brandy (2 small casks) and apple cider (8 large barrels) and cured them over winter
* Delivered them to the Winespring Inn every year in a horse drawn cart
* Children used to run loose in the forest
* Only a handful of farms can be found here dwindling from few to none just miles short of the Sand Hills
* It is said the land is too rocky
==== The al'Thor Farmstead ====
<br>
The house, barn and stone sheep pen all form the points of a triangle around the farmyard where chickens venture out from the barn. Beyond the fields outside of the farmyard, a tight-walled curing shed is built against the trees for drying tabac. A smokehouse, an open sheep shearing shed, and a well are also in the area of the farmyard. The vegetable garden is behind the house with more weeds than crop (cabbage, beans, pease, and beets). The vegetable garden is only partially planted. Most likely the residence also has apple trees and tabac fields, although this is not specifically mentioned in the book text. The Al'Thor's make their own apple brandy and apple cider. They also known to not be without dried tabac to sell when merchants come around.

==== The Farmhouse ====
<br>
The farmhouse is a neat rectangle with stout whitewashed wooden walls, windows facing the front and back, with no wings or additions. It has a steeply thatched roof. Stacks of pine firewood logs, many reaching all the way to the eaves are set against the side of the house. 
<br>
The house looks lived-in but clean and neat enough, warm, comforting, and cheerful. A broad oak table long enough to seat twelve with high-backed chairs is the main feature upon entry. There is also cushioned reading chir facing the large stone fireplace where a stew pot and a tea kettle hang over the flames. The main room is filled with several chairs and a bench to sit upon or hold piles of items being mended. Books have overflowed out onto chairs and side tables from the long book shelf and multiple candles are lit throughout. Off the main room is a backroom that exits to the farmyard, as well as having access to the stairway heading to the second floor with an attic storeroom and two bedrooms fitted up underneath the steep thatch roof.
<br>

* Not nearly so large as some of the sprawling farmhouses to the east - not big
* Most of the rooms on one floor
* A neat rectangle with no wings or additions
* Front windows
* Two bedrooms and an attic storeroom fitted up under the steeply sloped thatch.
* Whitewash (all but gone) on the stout wooden walls
* In a tidy state of repair, the thatch tightly mended and the doors and shutters well-hung and snug-fitting
* Stacks of Oak and Pine logs against the side of the house (many stacks) most reaching all the way to the eaves
===== Main room =====
* Big iron locks on the front and back doors
* Multiple candles (seemingly an extravagant amount)
* A fire crackled in the big stone fireplace with a stew pot over it and a small tea kettle hanging
* A bucket of water
* A cushioned reading chair sat angled before the flames
* A rug in front of the fire
* The main room had a warm, cheerful feel to it
* clean and neat enough, looked lived-in, warming and comforting
* A broad oaken table was the main feature - a table long enough to seat a dozen or more
* High-backed chairs standing around the table
* Wooden bowls and spoons for stew
* A few cabinets and chests, skillfully made by the homeowner lined the walls - with a waterbag in one
* A bookshelf by the door but not nearly as long as the one at the Winespring Inn
* A pitcher and basin on the washstand by the door
* A book sat on the table while another rested on the reading chair
* Bench by the fireplace with a harness to be mended on it
* Chair with shirts to be darned in a heap
* Sacks of Flour and Salt (unkown where they were kept in storage)
* A shuttered oil lantern
* Small bags of willowbark and medicines
===== Back room =====

===== Upstairs =====

* House, barn, and stone sheep pen formed the points of a triangle around the farmyard, where a few chickens had ventured out

== [[Quarry Road]] {{ref/book|1|1}}==
A rock-strewn track from the Westwood into the Two Rivers, worn from horse and cart wheels. It is surrounded by snarls of brambles over tight clumps of mostly bare trees with stone outcrops under them. Snow still dots patches in the shade.  Thorn covered nettles and stinkweed make up much of the brush. The surrounding area is now frequented by bears and wolves.  The forest gradually thins until the last few trees stand amongst the houses of Emond's Field.

* Rock-strewn track from the Westwood into the Two Rivers
* Worn from horse and cart wheels could be an added detail
* Snarls of brambles spread brown webs over stone outcrops under the trees
* Mostly Nettles amongst weeds with sharp burrs or thorns and stinkweed
* Scattered patches of white snow dotting the ground where tight clumps of trees kep deep shade
* Bare-branched trees offered no hiding place
* Wolves and Bears
* The forest gradually thinning until the last few trees stood actually among the houses

== [[Two Rivers]] {{ref/book|1|4}} {{ref/book|1|5}} ==
The Two Rivers consists of sprawling farmhouses in the villages of Emond's Field, Watch Hill, Taren Ferry, and Deven Ride. Most of the dwellings here had grown over time to hold entire extended families. To the west of Emond's Field, the land is fertile and holds lush pastures with only a handful of farms in an area called the Westwood. To the east, the land slopes gently down with patches of woods, farms, and hedge-bordered fields and pastures all the way to the Waterwood.
With the Mountains of Mist to the west, the Mire to the east, and the White River with the [[User_talk:Istalee82#Forest_of_Shadows_.5B3.5D_.5B12.5D|Forest of Shadows]] beyond it, no one would enter the Two Rivers except from the North, by way of Terren Ferry.

* Sprawling farmhouses - dwellings that had grown over the years to hold entire families
* Often included three or four generations under one roof, including aunts, uncles, cousins, and nephews
* Includes Emond's Field, Taren Ferry, Deven Ride, and Watch Hill
**Need to comb through Emond's Field for depictions that should have been for all of Two Rivers
* No one came into the two Rivers except from the north, by way of Taren Ferry.
* The Mountains of Mist, in the west, were the first, of course, and the Mire blocked the east just as effectively.
* To the south was the White River, which got its name from the way rocks and boulders churned its swift waters to froth.
* Beyond the White lay the Forest of Shadows
* Few Two Rivers folk had ever crossed the White, and fewer still returned if they did.
* It was generally agreed, though, that the Forest of Shadows stretched south for a hundred miles or more without a road or a village, but with plenty of wolves and bears.
=== [[Emond's Field]] {{ref/book|1|1}} ===
The village of Emond's Field is closest to the Westwood out of all of the Two Rivers' villages surrounding Quarry Road upon entry. It is home to several notable characters including Cenn Buie the thatcher (roofer), Wit Congar (town menace) with a dilapidated house and thatch roof in need of mending, Perrin Aybara's family's farm, Egwene al'Vere's family's residence, which is also the town's Inn and triples as the local governing body's meetinghouse, Matt Cauthon's family's residence located half-way up the green with a stone foundation and chimney, Master Luhhan's blacksmith's shop, and downstream of the Winespring you will find Master Thane's mill.

It is a busy village with Two Rivers folk hustling and bustling about stout framed houses repairing high-peaked thatch roofs, beating the dust out of sheets, rugs, and mattresses, and cooling fresh baked goods on window sills with broad shudders thrown open wide. 

It is a rocky land, yet fertile. Patches of woods, farms, and hedge-bordered fields and pastures quilt the land beyond the village all the way to the Waterwood. Within the center of Emond's Field is what is known as the Green.

* Eqwene house was the Mayor's
* Cenn Buie is the thatcher (find out if he has a farm close by or within the village)
* Wit Congar - damaged thatch, dilapidated house, wide front steps - enough to sprawl out on (lazy)
* The Aybara farm <u>(does the aybara farm have a forge on site?)</u>
* The Smithy
* Master Thane's mill - along the Winespring water between the Winespring and the Waterwood
* Close to the Westwood
* To the West - the land was just as fertile, and the pastures lush with only a handful of farms ( Westwood )
* To the East - Land sloping gently down
* Patches of woods, farms, and hedge-bordered fields and pastures quilted the land beyond the village all the way to the Waterwood
* Brown fields where crops should be sprouting and pastures greening
* Rocks everywhere
* High-peaked, thatched roofs surround Quarry Road upon entering the village
* Stout framed houses standing amongs the last few trees of the Westwood
* Leafless trees from a never ending winter
* Thatch roofs being repaired constantly from winter damage
* Broad shutters thrown back sheets or mattresses hanging over the windowsills (spring cleaning)
* Rugs hung from stretched lines (wicker beaters to clean them)
* Stools by kitchen fires baking pastries, honeycakes, or meat-pies
* Common under the houses were root cellars
* the street openes onto the Green, a broad expanse in the middle of the village
* <i>On "the edge" of the village is a smithy (blacksmith) - <b>which direction?</b></i> with a forge fire and tools being put up
* Matt Cauthons house half way up the green - stone foundations, a chimney (no further description)
==== [[Green]] {{ref/book|1|Ravens}} {{ref/book|1|1}} {{ref/book|1|3}} ==== 
The Green is a meadow ringed by a large wateroak, tall pine trees, as well as a hickory trees with tall shards of stones, possibly remnants of the mountains beyond, with some being as tall as the average man. The open area is used for the seasonal sheep shearing and festivals. Otherwise, a milk cow is usually tethered to crop the sparse grass and geese waddle about.
===== Night before the festival =====
* <i>A broad expanse in the middle of <b>Emond's Field (?) or the Two Rivers (?)</b></i> 
* Usually covered with thick grass, but now only showing a few fresh patches among the yellowish brown of dead grass and the black of bare earth
* Toward the west end of the Green is the Winespring coming out of a low stone outcrop.
* At the east stood The Winespring Inn, hard beside the Wagon Bridge
* Two low, railed footbridges crossed the clear stream at the Green, and one bridge wider than the others and stout enough to bear wagons
* The [[Wagon Bridge]] marks where the [[North Road]] coming down from Taren Ferry and Watch Hill, became the [[Old Road]], leading to Deven Ride
* The Wagon Bridge was made of heavy timbers
* On the far side of the bridges, the mounds were already building for the Bel Tine fires, three careful stacks of logs almost as big as houses on cleared dirt
* The [[Spring Pole]] is erected near the Winespring. Shorn of its branches, a straight, slender trunk of a fir tree - 10' tall at ground height, dug into the ground
* The Spring Pole is decorated with long colored ribbons to entwine it as the women dance
* A milk cow is tethered to crop the sparse growth
* Geese waddle about
* There are footraces and contests in archery, sling, and quarterstaff
* Contests solving riddles and puzzles, a rope tug, lifting and tossing weights, best singer, best dancer, best fiddle player, quickest to shear a sheep, bowls, and darts
* Also planned was a grand display of fireworks
* The night before Bel Tine everyone would visit and have a bite to eat and drink at every house
* Peddlers tall wagon drawn by eight horses with rounded canvas and bundles hanging off like grapes for a detail - sold pins, lace, books, needles, tea
===== At the shearing =====
* Meadow ringed by trees - usually empty most of the year but filled with sheep and people during the shearing.
* Large stones stuck out of the ground here and there, a few almost as tall as a man.
* Big, wooden-railed pens at the far end of the meadow held sheep already sheared, and others held those waiting to be washed.
* The pens are constructed of split wooden railings that did not conceal what was within or behind them well
* A large dog stands in front of one of the pens. Close, curly gray coat and intelligent eyes. Very big, almost waist-high to a grown man
* There is a large pen holding shorn sheep almost to the trees on the Waterwood side of the meadow.
* There is also a large black sheep-dog there
* Noteable that this pen is where Rand and his group of friends would hide to get out of doing work.
* The fleece was carried to the slatted tables by men where women sorted the wool and folded it for bailing.
* There are areas where wool that needs to be washed again are set aside.
* Women kept tally and labeled so that no one's wool was mixed with anyone else's.
* Long trestle tables were set with food along the trees to the left (Egwenes viewpoint coming in with water from the Winespring).
* Everything was displayed - from roast goose to honeycakes.
* Tea water boiling on fires behind the tables.
* There is a notable sized "big wateroak" and a row of tall pine trees, as well as a hickory - a mixed border in the area of the trestle tables
* There was an area where the wisdom would tend to those needing medical attention. They would sit on logs.
* Wool-Shears could be an added detail to the area.
* Notable that the shepherds would have a sling or a bow always at the ready to protect against wolves or bears.

==== [[Winespring Water]] {{ref/book|1|Ravens}} {{ref/book|1|1}} ====

Toward the west end of the Green, the Winespring gushes out of a low stone outcrop in a flow that never fails.  It is strong enough to knock a man down before widening into the Winespring Water and running swiftly off to the east. Willows dot its banks all the way to Master Thane's mill and beyond as it then splits into dozens of streams in the swampy depths of the Waterwood. Two low-railed foot bridges cross the clear stream from the Green. Then halfway to the Waterwood stands mostly willows and one single large Whitewood Tree near the knee-deep water where sheep are washed to be sheared.

* Toward the west end of the Green, it gushed out of a low stone outcrop in a flow that never failed (known here as the Winspring)
* Its flow was strong enough to knock a man down
* It rapidly widens into the Winespring Water and runs swiftly off to the east
* Willows dotting its banks all the way to Master Thane's mill and beyond
* It then splits into dozens of streams in the swampy depths of the Waterwood
* Two low, railed foot bridges cross the clear stream at the Green (refer to the Green)
* Below Emond's Field and halfway to the Waterwood, trees lined the banks of the Winespring Water. 
* Mostly willows, their leafy branches made a shady canopy over the water near the bank.
* 100 paces further down river men stood knee-deep washing sheep to be sheared.
* The Whinespring Water did not flow as swiftly here as it did in Emond's Field, yet it was not slow.
* There is a notable sized single whitewood tree near where the men were washing sheep.

In the Waterwood east of Emond's Field, which consists of a tangle of ponds and streams children climb trees and swim. At the far end is the Mire, which is full of quicksands and bogs.

==== [[The Winespring Inn]] {{ref/book|1|2}}{{ref/book|1|4}} {{ref/book|1|7}} {{ref/book|1|8}} {{ref/book|1|9}} {{ref/book|1|10}} ====

The Winespring Inn is located beside the Wagon Bridge at the east end of the Green within Emond's Field. Tripling as an inn, the mayor and his family's residence, the mayor's office, and meetingplace for the Village Council, it is a very prominent building and is said it has been there for 1,000 years or more. It's foundation is of an older stone said to have come from the mountains, with the first floor being river rock, and the second story being whitewashed. It also has the only red tile roof in the village with 12 tall chimneys standing proud of the roof, it is very hospitable with a fireplace in each room. Where the mayor resides is jutted out over the lower floor all the way around at the back of the inn. As with most businesses, it also comes equipped with a stables and stablemen for travelers.

On the south end, away from the stream, stretches the remains of a much larger stone foundation, believed to once have been part of the inn. A huge oak grows in the middle of it with a bole thirty paces around. In the summer, tables and benches are set under the branches for patrons to drink beverages or play a board game called stones.

* Mayors home (also is the innkeeper - [[Egwene al'Vere]]'s Father)
* Stands hard beside the Wagon Bridge at the east end of the Green
* The foundation is of older stone (poss from the mountains)
* The first floor of the inn is river rock
* The second story is Whitewashed
* The Mayor and family lived in the back - jutted out over the lower floor all the way around
* Red roof tile (the only such roof in the village)
* Smoke drifts from 3 of the 12 tall chimneys
* Has been there for 1,000 years, maybe more, it is said
* On the south end, away from the stream, stretched the remains of a much larger stone foundation
* Believed to once be part of the inn
* A huge oak grew in the middle of it with a bole thirty paces around
* (In summer) tables and benches are set under the branches for patrons to drink beverages or a play a board game called stones
* The scales used to weigh coins of merchants visiting from Baerlon for wool or tabac, was the symbol of the Mayor's office
* Cider goes into the cellar
* <i>The Inn has Stablemen - <b>where is the stable?</b></i>
===== Common Room =====

Upon entry into the common room, patrons are served drinks from casks racked against the wall and baked goods from the kitchens. In the big square common room there is a large fireplace of river rock and a stone mantel stretching half the legnth, the lintel as high as a man's shoulder. Placed in front are enough high-backed chairs to hold a board meeting where as many as 8 large men can gather at once. There are book shelves opposite the fireplace and small tables to play stones throughout.

Through the doorway at the back of the common room you will enter a hall that leads to the kitchen, the stairs down to the cellar by the kitchen door, and stairs leading up to the rooms. Baked bread, trays of crusty loaves, plates of pickles and cheese, and honeycakes are offered fresh from these kitchens. Then a door leads out of the rear of the kitchen toward the stable yard.

* casks are racked against one wall (with a yellow cat)

* Stretches half the length of the big, square room, with a lintel as high as a man's shoulder with a hearth holding a crackling blaze

===== Stable =====
The Stable is a long narrow building with a high-peaked thatch roof.  There is potential for approximately 18 stalls with 9 on either side and there are double doors on either end.  Nails on stall posts are placed to hang lanterns and there is a hayloft with a ladder leading up to it.  One side exits out onto the stablyard, down the bank through the willows and into the Winespring Water to the far bank, devoid of any village houses.

== [[Baerlon]] {{ref/book|1|13}}{{ref/book|1|14}}==
* One week's travel from the Forest of Shadows to Baerlon

* The road passing half a dozen farms on the way to the gates

* A 20ft tall log wall surrounds the town
* Wooden watchtowers scattered along its length

* A frayed rope hangs down beside the gates clanging a bell on the opposite side
* A guard looks between the cut-off ends of two logs a good three spans over the visitors heads

== [[Tar Valon]] {{ref/book|1|9}} ==
* An island in the middle of a broad river which flowed by the mountain
* A city surrounded by high gleaming white and silver-streaked walls

* Soaring towers joined by walkways that spanned the open air
* High arching bridges from both banks of the river to the island city
* Lacy (intricate) stonework on the spans (bridges), too delicate to withstand the swift waters that rushed beneath them
* There was no building, no monument that did not make a man stare
* Stone and brick and tile had been used to create beauty awed by mortals
* The street entering the city is broad and paved with smooth grey stone straight toward the center of the city
* At the center is the White Tower
* Narrow side street containing street markets selling fruit
* The White Tower rises out of a huge square in the middle of the city 
==== [[The White Tower]] {{ref/book|1|Ravens}} {{ref/book|1|9}} ====
* Taller than anything but a mountain.
* The tower loomed, larger and taller than any other in the city
* White as fresh-fallen snow
* Rising from a great palace of pale marble, sculpted rather than built, curving walls and swelling domes and delicate spires fingering the sky
* Broad stairs of pristine stone leads up from the square
* Scrollwork covers the massive doors at the top of the stairs, carvings so intricate and delicate that a knife blade was not fine enough to fit
== [[Tear]] {{ref/book|1|13}} ==
* A city all the way down on the Sea of Storms
* The greatest port on the Sea of Storms
* The stone of Tear is the fortress that guards it
* The stone is said to be the first fortress built after the Breaking of the World
* In all this time it has never fallen though more than one army has tried
* The Sword That Cannot Be Touched lies in the Heart of the Stone
* The Heart of the stone is the central citadel of the fortress
===== RPG notes =====
Profecies say: 
* The Stone of Tear will never fall until the People of the Dragon come
* The stone will never fall till the Sword That Cannot Be Touched is wielded by the Dragon's Hand
* The fall of the Stone will be one of the major proofs that the Dragon has been reborn.
* None but the High Lords of Tear can enter the Heart of the Stone
* Hates anything to do with the Power even more than Amador

== [[Amador]] {{ref/book|1|13}} ==
* the stronghold of the Children of the Light


== [[Shayol Ghul]] ==

== [[Dragonmount]] {{ref/book|1|Prologue}} ==
* Molten rock fountaining five hundred feet into the air, and the groaning ground rose, thrusting the burning spray ever upward, ever higher. From north and south, from east and west, the wind howled in, snapping trees like twigs, shrieking and blowing as if to aid the growing mountain ever skyward. Ever skyward.
* Where Lews Therin Telamon had stood a mountain now rose miles into the sky, molten lava still gushing from its broken peak. The broad straight river had been pushed into a curve away from the mountain, and there it split to form a long island in its midst. The shadow of the mountain almost reached the island; it lay dark across the land like the ominous hand of prophecy. For a time the dull, protesting rumbles of the earth were the only sound.
* On the island, the air shimmered and coalesced. Looking toward the fiery mountain rising out of the plain. And there, they stood alone. Waiting.
